chats.answer:
Look for a charger with a real-time per-port power display, not just a screen showing total wattage. These three are confirmed matches:

Anker 140W 4-Port Charger (A2697)

$53.99

B&H Photo

My pick for a wall charger. Press its touch control once to see separate live watt readings for all three USB-C ports and the USB-A port, plus the total. Its 140W capacity is shared across devices. 
Manuals+

Anker Prime 250W 6-Port Charger (A2345)

$149.99

Anker-US

Best for a desk with multiple laptops. Its 2.26-inch screen shows all four USB-C wattages together, and a dial lets you prioritize ports. It also has two USB-A ports, but I could only confirm individual on-screen readings for USB-C. 
Macworld
+1

UGREEN Nexode Pro 100W 4-Port Smart Display Charger

$54.99

UGREEN

A lower-power alternative with more diagnostic detail: tap through screens for each port's watts, volts and amps, as well as the charging protocol. Make sure you select the Smart Display version. 
UGREEN US
+1

I'd choose the Anker A2697 unless you need more than 140W combined. I used US listings and verified the display behavior from manuals or reviews, rather than testing the chargers myself. One limitation applies to all of them: the reading is power leaving the charger port, not the exact power reaching the device's battery after cable losses and the device's own power consumption.

chats.answer:
These four chargers have built-in displays that show live wattage for each connected port, not just the charger's combined output. I focused on multi-device chargers where that distinction is explicitly documented.

Anker 140W 4-Port Charger with Built-In Screen

$53.99

B&H Photo

Wall charger; 3 USB-C and 1 USB-A. Its screen shows individual port wattages, total output, and temperature. Two USB-C ports can supply 70W each together. The screen sleeps after one minute. 
B&H Photo Video

UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port (X774)

$56.99

Best Buy

Wall charger; 4 USB-C and 1 USB-A. The display shows wattage for multiple ports simultaneously, plus total output; another screen shows voltage and current. An independent test demonstrated 98W on C1 and 55W on C2. 
ChargerLAB

Satechi ChargeView 140W Desktop Charger

$74.99

B&H Photo

Desktop charger with 4 USB-C ports and a live per-port wattage display. A good fit if you want the readout visible on your desk rather than down at an outlet.

Satechi ChargeView 240W Desktop Charger

$149.99

B&H Photo

6 USB-C ports and 240W shared output. Its on-demand LCD shows each port's wattage and the total; C1 and C2 each support up to 140W individually. Best suited to a desk with several high-power devices. 
Macworld

I'd choose the UGREEN X774 for a wall charger because its simultaneous per-port readout is particularly well verified, or the Satechi 140W for a desk. Note that these displays measure power leaving the charger, not power reaching a device's battery after cable losses and the device's own consumption.

I used US listings and assumed you wanted the display on the charger itself. I haven't tested the chargers or their meter accuracy, and retailer prices may change.
